business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Trade Intermediary and Commercial Re-Invoicing Operations

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Beneficial owner registration is governed by the Market Entity Beneficial Owner Registration Administration Measures (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024), the Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision), the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), the Limited Partnership Funds Ordinance (Cap. 637), the Hong Kong Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), and the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) for economic substance and resident/offshore claims.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route only: notarize the certificate or certified extract, then obtain a Hong Kong High Court apostille. No consular legalization and no sequential chain with the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry / official registry extract office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route only: notarized copy accompanied by an apostille issued by the High Court of the HKSAR; consular legalization is not used for member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General partner or corporate director body of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route only: notarize the signatories' identity and capacity, then apostillize the resolution/power of attorney in Hong Kong; never add consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Constituent constitutional document registered with the Hong Kong Companies Registry / applicable partnership instrument
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route only: certified copy plus notarization plus High Court apostille; no consular chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The relationship bank holding the proposed re-invoicing account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route only: notarize the authorized bank officer's signature and letterhead, then obtain apostille from the High Court of the HKSAR; do not chain consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every natural-person beneficial owner, general partner, authorized signatory, and agent must be screened pre-incorporation and continuously against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK HMT sanctions list, China's Ministry of Public Security and MOFCOM sanctions measures, Interpol notices, and the Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department's terrorist-financing watch links. PEPs, their family members and close associates must receive enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, with negative news monitoring conducted every 30 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) and, for the mainland China FIP registration limb, the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) / SAMR Enterprise Name Registration Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Hong Kong names may be in English, Traditional Chinese, or bilingual; exact-name and similarity checks are operated by ICRIS. Mainland Foreign-Invested Partnership names must follow the four-tier structure: administrative district + distinctive trade name + industry/scope + organizational form, using simplified Chinese characters. Foreign partner names may be transliterated phonetically only when the resulting distinctive element is not confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise or protected mark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, obtain the written refusal stating the statutory ground and the registry case number. Within 15 working days of refusal, submit a formal appeal to the Registry's Name Review Officer or the SAMR Name-Routing Review Office. The appeal must include the name-search report, a comparison table, evidence of lawful authorization for any sensitive token, and, where relevant, a declaration of acquired distinctiveness. If the first-level appeal is refused, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration within 60 days and thereafter may initiate judicial review in the competent court, while preserving the priority date through a fresh name reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A bare virtual-office or commercial-mailbox address is rejected by HK banks and the mainland tax authorities for a re-invoicing entity because the ISIC 4690 operation requires demonstrable transaction management, contractual execution, and bank settlement substance. The permissible arrangement is a serviced/physical registered office with a real inactive desk, local mail receiving staff, board/partner meeting capacity, and original accounting or transaction records available at the address. A purely virtual arrangement will not satisfy the Inland Revenue Ordinance source test and will increase the likelihood of a PE assessment for the Hong Kong leg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) in-force lease or license for the registered office; (2) utility charges or service bills addressed to the entity; (3) local management personnel or an authorized representative able to produce records at the site; (4) statutory registers, minutes, and partnership ledgers; (5) re-invoicing contracts, purchase orders, invoices, and SWIFT/TT/XT payment records; (6) bank statements evidencing economic routing; (7) annual reporting and business registration proofs. Quantified risk: 35-45% probability of an unannounced inspection within 24 months for a high-volume re-invoicing hub, increasing to over 50% if the registered office is a virtual mailbox or agent-only address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38), ss. 3-4 and 17-22; Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 337), ss. 4-11; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), s. 5; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), Sch. 2
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Limited Partnerships Registration Section; Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership) and IRBR Form 1 (Business Registration Application)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong partnership law imposes no minimum paid-up capital, no capital verification certificate, and no blocked escrow account requirement. Partners are free to agree capital contributions, profit shares and loss shares in the partnership agreement, and funds may be held in ordinary operating accounts once the partnership is registered.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST GOVERNING BODY RESOLUTION (FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION) OF CN_FIP; WHEREAS the Partnership is to be constituted as a limited partnership registered in Hong Kong under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance Cap. 337 and the Partnership Ordinance Cap. 38; WHEREAS it shall conduct general re-invoicing and offshore trade intermediation under ISIC 4690 and may use SWIFT LC, TT wire and cross-border payment platforms; NOW THEREFORE, the General Partners unanimously resolve as follows: 1. Formation and Registered Office: The registration of CN_FIP under Cap. 337 is approved; the registered office and principal place of business shall be such address in Hong Kong as specified in the Registration Certificate; the Partnership shall keep there its statutory books, registers, contracts, invoices and payment records, and shall use that office for all correspondence and service of process until changed by a supplementary resolution. 2. Capital Subscription: Given that the Partnership is not a company and has no share capital, the partners subscribe to the partnership capital and capital accounts set out in the Contribution Schedule; Hong Kong law imposes no minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow requirement, but funds must be credited to the Partnership's bank account and recorded in partner capital statements within 30 days of receipt. 3. Banking Authorization: The General Partner is authorized to open and maintain the Partnership's operating account at a licensed bank; to execute all account mandates, KYC declarations, SWIFT and telex instructions; to receive letters of credit and invoice-generated trade payments; to sign indemnities and treasury forms; and to initiate TT wires up to USD 50,000; an amount above USD 50,000 requires dual signatory authorization and post-controller review. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments: [Designated Representative] is appointed as designated partner and statutory representative for business registration, tax filing, and liaison with the Companies Registry and Inland Revenue Department; [Compliance Officer] is appointed as anti-money-laundering reporting officer and is charged with maintaining the beneficial ownership, transaction-monitoring and record-keeping framework under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance. 5. This resolution is unconditional and effective upon registration; each partner, officer, agent, banker and professional adviser may rely upon it; it shall remain in force until revoked by a subsequent unanimous written resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability and Partnership Agreement Preparatory Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR - Cyber Search Centre online name search portal; Intellectual Property Department online trademark search service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search through the Companies Registry's public computer index to confirm that the proposed Chinese and English firm name is not the same as or too similar to an existing Hong Kong company or limited partnership. Verify separate legal availability on the Cyber Search Centre. Confirm no registered trademark conflict by consulting the Intellectual Property Department online mark search. Prepare the partnership agreement and confirm the designated representative, principal place of business, capital amount, and profit-share/loss-share allocations. No fee is payable for search; statutory fee is paid on Form LP1. If name is occupied, select suffix such as 'International', 'Asia-Pacific', or a unique geographic modifier and rerun search.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name in English and/or Chinese
Name search results from Cyber Search Centre
Trademark search results from Intellectual Property Department
Draft limited partnership agreement signed by general partners
Capital contribution schedule and profit-loss allocation schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is objected by the Companies Registry or a third-party trademark holder, file an amended Form LP1 under a revised name, obtain a consent letter from the prior registrant or trademark owner, or add a distinctive distinctive element to the firm name before resubmitting the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registration of Limited Partnership with Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR - Limited Partnerships Registration Section, e-Registry portal online filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form LP1 in English or Chinese from the Companies Registry website indicating the firm name, nature of business (ISIC 4690 general re-invoicing and offshore trade intermediation), registered office address, names and addresses of all partners, and statement of capital. Every general partner must sign in the presence of a witness; limited partners must sign the declaration of limited liability. The form and each partner's current residential address and passport copy must be enclosed; non-HK residents must provide an overseas address and a recent utility/bank statement. Submit online via e-Registry or in person at the counter. The Registrar will issue a Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership upon approval. If requisitioned, file an amended Form LP1 with additional evidence and any consent letters.
required_dossiers: Completed Form LP1 signed by all general partners and witnessed
Certified copy of the limited partnership agreement
Passport or national identity document of every general and limited partner
Proof of residential address for each partner (utility bill, bank statement or notarized address declaration)
Proof of principal place of business or registered office address in Hong Kong (lease or tenancy agreement)
Payment of the prescribed Companies Registry filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry issues a requisition under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance, answer within 14 calendar days with an amended Form LP1 and supporting declarations. Defective signatures must be re-executed before a notary public or made at the Companies Registry, and a revised statement of capital must be filed if the Registrar queries the contribution or liability structure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration Certificate from Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office - online Business Registration e-Services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the limited partnership is registered (or commencement of business, whichever is earlier), apply to the Business Registration Office using IRBR Form 1. Submit the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership, the partnership agreement, the identity documents of the general partner or managing partner, and proof of the Hong Kong registered address. The office will issue a Business Registration Certificate bearing a file number, and the partnership becomes subject to the annual Business Registration fee and levy under Cap. 310. Post the certificate in the registered office and state the certificate number on invoices and letterheads. If application is late, pay the prescribed late fee and request a certificate of non-assessment; if refused, appeal in writing within 14 days under section 8 of Cap. 310.
required_dossiers: IRBR Form 1 completed and signed
Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Identity document of the designated general partner or managing partner
Lease or tenancy agreement for the Hong Kong registered office
Annual Business Registration fee and levy payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Office withholds the certificate due to late filing or incomplete data, pay the prescribed late fee, file the missing IRBR Form 1 pages, and provide written reasons for delay. If the certificate is refused, appeal in writing to the Inland Revenue Board of Review and request a temporary document of compliance pending the statutory determination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and AML/KYC Post-Registration Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Independent licensed bank in Hong Kong acting under the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance; licensed bank AML compliance unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a commercial multi-currency bank account at the selected licensed bank under the partnership name. Present the original limited partnership certificate, business registration certificate, signed partnership agreement, and the first-board resolution or general partner resolution authorizing banking officers. Complete the bank's anti-money-laundering and know-your-customer questionnaire, submit ultimate beneficial ownership declarations and source-of-funds evidence, and provide the corporate chart and expected transaction flows. If the bank queries beneficial ownership or transaction profile, supply an updated partnership register and a cascaded AML/KYC pack. After account opening, route all LC, TT, and cross-border telex transfers through authorized signatories, with expected SLA of 7-10 business days for approval and issuance of tins/cards/tokens.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Business Registration Certificate
Limited partnership agreement and pro-forma first governing body resolution
AML/KYC forms and ultimate beneficial ownership declaration
Source of funds and source of wealth evidence for all partners
Corporate chart and expected re-invoicing transaction flow description
Bank account application and authorized signatory forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends account opening, strengthen the UBO evidence pack, provide sample invoices and purchase orders illustrating the re-invoicing model, and complete any additional FATF-compliant questionnaires. If ultimately declined, wait 30 days and approach a second licensed bank with an enhanced compliance pack prepared by a professional legal or accounting adviser.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 4690 is a non-industrial, non-manufacturing re-invoicing and offshore trade intermediation operation; no industrial licensing board is triggered. The only fiscal operating authorization is issued by the Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no operating or manufacturing permit is required beyond the Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance and the registration as a limited partnership under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, VOC emission, hazardous waste generation, or physical process exists; the activity does not meet the threshold for an Environmental Impact Assessment study, an environmental permit, or an environmental registration under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - pure office-based commercial re-invoicing operations require no Civil Defense fire certification, no structural load inspection, and no industrial workplace safety approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance. If the registered office later includes a physical warehouse or sampling room, a mandatory fire service installation certificate and a building fire safety compliance certificate will be required from the Hong Kong Fire Services Department and Buildings Department.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, with electronic filing via the China Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax) at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn; Hong Kong SAR activities are separately supervised by the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) through its Business Registration Office and eTax portal at https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/ese/.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the PRC foreign-invested partnership (FIP), the process begins with registration under the Foreign Investment Law and the Partnership Enterprise Law with the local authority for market regulation (for example, the Municipal Administration for Market Regulation in the relevant pilot-free-trade zone). Upon issuance of the business license, the FIP automatically receives an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which constitutes its national tax identification number (TIN) for VAT, corporate income tax withholding, customs, and export tax rebate purposes. The USCC is synchronised to the STA through the multi-license integration system, so no separate TIN application is required. The FIP must then complete VAT taxpayer registration with the competent state tax bureau, selecting either small-scale taxpayer status when annual taxable turnover does not exceed CNY 5,000,000, or general VAT taxpayer status to issue VAT special invoices and claim export refunds. For export activity, the FIP must obtain a customs registration code from the General Administration of Customs via the China International Trade Single Window and complete the export tax rebate filing registration with the STA. Non-resident partners that do not hold a PRC TIN must separately register for a non-resident taxpayer identification number through the STA e-Tax platform before the partnership income tax distribution return is filed. For any Hong Kong presence or parallel Hong Kong partnership, a Business Registration Certificate must be obtained from the IRD Business Registration Office, and the registration number serves as the Hong Kong taxpayer reference.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under PRC law, because the FIP is automatically treated as fiscally transparent under the Partnership Enterprise Law and Caishui [2008] No. 159; each partner is taxed on the distributive share of partnership income. No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election is available in the PRC. The FIP may, however, elect between small-scale VAT taxpayer status and general VAT taxpayer status when eligible, and may elect simplified VAT calculation for certain services. In Hong Kong, no partnership-level profits tax election exists; the partnership is also transparent and partners are separately assessed under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: People's Republic of China Value-Added Tax (VAT); note that Hong Kong SAR imposes no general VAT, GST, or sales tax, so PRC VAT is the applicable indirect tax for mainland taxable supplies by the FIP.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 annual aggregate taxable turnover, above which registration as a PRC general VAT taxpayer is mandatory; below this threshold the FIP may remain a small-scale taxpayer unless voluntary general registration is elected.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices must be issued through the STA-controlled Unified VAT Invoice System (tax-control equipment and the fully digital electronic invoice platform). Invoices are transmitted in real time to the STA with digital encryption and online verification, and are matched through the VAT Invoice Comprehensive Service Platform. The Golden Tax Phase IV system performs continuous anti-fraud and risk analytics. Export declarations must be transmitted through the China International Trade Single Window, which links customs, tax, foreign exchange, and bank data. The FIP must reconcile each export with the corresponding electronic invoice, customs declaration, and receipt of foreign exchange before claiming a zero-rating or refund benefit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under PRC VAT Law and implementing regulations, exports of physical goods are zero-rated and eligible for the VAT export refund (exemption, credit, and refund method) for general VAT taxpayers if: the goods are declared and physically exported through a PRC customs checkpoint; the FIP has completed export tax rebate filing before the export; the export transaction is real, the commercial documents are authentic, and the foreign exchange payment is received and repatriated to a PRC bank account within the statutory period. Re-invoicing of goods that never enter PRC customs territory (offshore trade or direct delivery from a foreign supplier) does not qualify for PRC export zero-rating and may fall outside PRC VAT altogether; any such claim would be treated as fraudulent and clawed back. In the Hong Kong SAR context, offshore trading profits may be exempt from profits tax, but that is a direct-tax relief separate from VAT zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (outbound goods declaration) electronically recorded by the General Administration of Customs via the China International Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading, airway bill, or multimodal transport document issued by the independent carrier
Foreign exchange receipt certificate (inward remittance certificate) issued by a PRC-designated bank, demonstrating repatriation of export proceeds in convertible currency
Commercial invoice, packing list, and the underlying sale/purchase contracts
VAT special invoice received from the upstream PRC supplier to substantiate the input VAT credit used in the refund calculation
Export tax refund application filing receipt and any customs verification printout generated by the e-Tax or Single Window system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the PRC Tax Administration Law (Article 66) and Criminal Law (Article 204), fraudulent or baseless export zero-rating claims trigger immediate clawback of the refund, daily late-payment interest of 0.05% of the clawed-back amount, and an administrative penalty of one to five times the amount fraudulently obtained. The STA and General Administration of Customs cross-check export declarations, bills of lading, VAT invoices, and foreign-exchange receipts through Golden Tax Phase IV and the Trade Single Window; any false document, circular transaction, unverified transport, or failure to repatriate foreign exchange within the prescribed deadline leads to retroactive cancellation of zero-rating, recovery of refunds with penalties, suspension or revocation of export refund eligibility, and referral to criminal authorities. In severe cases, individual participants may be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment, up to life imprisonment. Hong Kong IRD separately applies anti-avoidance and penalty provisions of the Inland Revenue Ordinance to false offshore-profits claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the Hong Kong SAR central banking authority; People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for mainland Chinese cross-border capital flows
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Hong Kong SAR operates as a separate monetary jurisdiction with a fully convertible currency, the Hong Kong dollar, linked to the United States dollar through the Linked Exchange Rate System. The HKMA imposes no foreign exchange controls, no surrender requirements, and no restrictions on the repatriation of profits, capital, dividends, or partnership distributions for legally formed entities operating in Hong Kong. However, the owning shareholders or partners that are resident in mainland China remain subject to mainland China's Foreign Exchange Administration Rules and SAFE supervision when injecting capital into or receiving distributions from the Hong Kong FIP. Current account items such as trade settlements, service fees, and reasonable surrogate payments are generally permissible without SAFE prior approval, while capital account items including direct investment, acquisition of equity or partnership interests, and cross-border funding require SAFE registration, ODI filing, or other ad hoc approvals. The practical challenge for the FIP is not the Hong Kong convertibility but the upstream Chinese outbound investment compliance; the FIP must maintain full documentation of the Chinese parent's capital remittance route, including the SAFE ODI certificate, the capital verification report issued by a PRC certified public accountant, and the source of funds declaration for each partner. Profit repatriation from Hong Kong to China can be executed freely by the Hong Kong FIP, but the Chinese recipient must ensure that the inward remittance falls within an approved quota and that any required PRC enterprise income tax holding or tax filing is satisfied. For a re-invoicing business, funds frequently flow into Hong Kong from overseas buyers or from mainland Chinese procurement entities. While the Hong Kong FIP itself enjoys full convertibility, the bank and the AML compliance team will expect a clear economic substance trail, including contractual obligations, trade documentation, freight forwarding records, and payment timing logic, to avoid the characterization of illegal cross-border arbitrage or round-tripping. Overall, the regime is open and flexible for the Hong Kong entity, but the governing constraint is the heightened scrutiny of trade-based money laundering risks inherent in a general re-invoicing hub model.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Hong Kong imposes no export proceeds surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory timeline for retaining foreign currency receipts. The Hong Kong FIP may maintain USD, HKD, EUR, or CNY accounts and schedule outbound payments freely. However, where the underlying sales are booked by a mainland Chinese affiliate, SAFE requires the Chinese exporter to repatriate export proceeds through the Chinese banking system within the prescribed time frame and to observe any applicable forced conversion ratio if the proceeds are held in a restricted category. This blueprint is written specifically for the Hong Kong FIP, and therefore no surrender obligation attaches to the Hong Kong treasury activity.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (HSBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account with Trade Finance Facilities
Basic Operational Currency Account and Multi-currency Settlements
Basic Operational Currency Account and Commercial Re-Invoicing Sub-Accounts

stage_4.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Hong Kong permits licensed fintech EMIs, Money Service Operators, and Stored Value Facilities to offer multi-currency digital accounts to corporates. For this FIP, a fintech EMI such as Airwallex or Currenxie can provide fast cross-border payment rails, virtual IBANs, and flexible FX conversion, and is not legally barred from servicing Hong Kong entities. However, the viability rating decreases for the primary treasury host because a mainland Chinese partner injecting capital or receiving repatriations will generally prefer a licensed Tier-1 commercial bank to satisfy SAFE documentation and to provide conventional trade finance instruments such as letters of credit. A fintech EMI may be used as a secondary disbursement vehicle for small-value supplier payments, contingent on robust KYC and a clear audit trail, but it should not replace the primary settlement bank for capital account transactions, commercial letters of credit, or operations requiring a formal physical branch nexus and SWIFT direct membership. The legal constraint is not entity eligibility but the ability to evidence the beneficial ownership structure and the source of funds through an EMI's automated onboarding, which often has lower tolerance for bespoke re-invoicing structures. The final recommendation is to maintain the Tier-1 commercial bank as the liquidity core, with a fintech EMI positioned on a trial basis for ancillary cross-border vendor disbursements only after the bank compliance committee has approved the full corporate structure.
stage_4.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under HKMA AML guidelines, a Hong Kong corporate account for a foreign-invested partnership with non-Hong Kong partners generally requires the general partner and a designated signatory to attend an in-branch KYC interview at the chosen Tier-1 commercial bank. Remote video interviews and consular proxy openings are sometimes accepted by individual relationship managers under enhanced due diligence, but approval is discretionary and depends on the bank's risk appetite for trade-intermediary structures. For the highest onboarding viability, the general partner should plan physical attendance in Hong Kong during account opening, bringing original partnership certificate, valid passports, proof of Hong Kong registered address, and source of funds documents. If remote opening is unavoidable, the bank may accept a notarized power of attorney issued through a Hong Kong solicitor or a mainland Chinese notary office, plus a video call with a compliance officer, but this does not eliminate the need for the ultimate beneficial owners to submit certified identification and address proofs. The safest path is a full in-person branch interview for the physical representative and a rigorous beneficial ownership declaration for every mainland Chinese partner holding ten percent or more of the FIP capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multiple mainland Chinese partners with complex ownership layers trigger the bank's Politically Exposed Persons and beneficial ownership identification red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an organizational chart showing every partner, their direct and indirect percentages, audited partnership agreement, HK Business Registration certificate, CRS self-certification forms, certified passport copies, and a notarized declaration explaining the commercial purpose of each partner's participation in the FIP, signed and dated by the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Re-invoicing trade model with goods shipped directly from mainland China to third-country buyers raises trade-based money laundering concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble a transaction-matching evidence file containing the original master sales contracts, the re-invoicing purchase agreements, bills of lading or airway bills, customs declarations, warehouse receipts, inspection certificates, and an invoice flow map demonstrating the margin structure and the payment settlement terms among the mainland supplier, the Hong Kong FIP, and the final buyer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound equity injections from mainland China to the Hong Kong FIP may be scrutinized as unauthorized round-tripping or disguised capital flight
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the SAFE Outbound Direct Investment (ODI) certificate, the PRC foreign exchange registration letter, the FIC / enterprise income tax filing acknowledgement, a capital verification report issued by a licensed accountant, board minutes approving the capital call, source of funds attestation, and a capital utilization plan showing the funds will be applied to specific trade settlements and operational expenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent payouts to unverified third-country suppliers or related mainland entities can appear as layering or anomalous value flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle KYC files for each material counterparty, including business registration, US / EU / Asia tax identification or VAT numbers, signed supplier agreements, due diligence questionnaires, utility bills or address verification, and a payment trail reconciling each outbound transaction to commercial invoices, goods arrival evidence, and signed acknowledgment of receipt from the beneficiary.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate Renewal (Application for Business Registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after expiry of the current one-year certificate or at the end of the current three-year certificate; anniversary date is the original business registration date and renewal is due annually if the one-year option is selected.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts a statutory penalty of approximately HK$300 (USD 38.40). Continued non-renewal is an offence under the Business Registration Ordinance with a maximum fine of HK$5,000 (USD 640.00) and imprisonment up to one year; the Business Registration Office may also cancel the certificate and administratively strike the FIP from the active business register, which will impair bank payment rails and the FT/LC issuance capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for Partnership (Form BIR52) together with Financial Statements and Tax Computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the date of issue of the profits tax return, normally issued in April or May for partnerships with a 31 December accounting date; a hold-over extension of up to three months may be granted on written application by the tax representative.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in a maximum penalty of HK$10,000 (USD 1,280.00) plus additional penalties of treble the tax undercharged where misleading returns are filed. The IRD may issue estimated assessments and impose default surcharges of 5% on tax unpaid after six months and an additional 10% on tax unpaid after twelve months; continued failure to comply can trigger administrative enforcement against the partnership registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Annual Return of Remuneration and Pensions (BIR56A) and Employee's Particulars (BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - Employer Returns Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 1 May each year for the year of assessment ended 31 March; electronic filing may be required where the FIP has multiple employees.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse may attract a fine of up to HK$10,000 (USD 1,280.00) and, if tax is thereby undercharged, additional liability to three times the tax undercharged. Subsequent prosecution and administrative enforcement may follow; the IRD may take the FIP as a billing and compliance default and escalate to business deregistration action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notification of Change of Partnership Particulars, Partners, Capital Contributions, and Registered Business Particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry (for a limited partnership registered under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance Cap. 37) and Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office (for business registration particulars)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 days of any change in partner identity, capital contribution profile, residence/service address, or registered particulars under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance; within one month of change for business registration particulars.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance may expose the general partner to fines and daily default fines and the Registrar may administratively deregister a defunct partnership; inaccuracies in business registration particulars can result in late-notification penalties and suspension of the Business Registration Certificate, causing interruption of banking and settlement links for the re-invoicing trade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/KYC and Beneficial Ownership Confirmation to the Registered Office or Corporate Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBP) service provider and any licensed bank maintaining Swift_LC or TT_Wire settlement rails
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at each calendar year-end and within 30 days of any transfer of partnership interests or change in ultimate beneficial owner; clients on medium-risk enhanced due diligence require confirmation before each significant new trade counterparty.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No statutory government strike-off is triggered, but breach of AML/KYC onboarding or enhanced monitoring terms may lead the registered agent to resign, the bank to terminate the account, and trade credit lines to be withdrawn; this materially impairs the general re-invoicing hub and may expose the general partner to breach of the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance Cap. 615 where the FIP is within the DNFBP sector.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maintenance and Retention of Statutory Books and Records in Hong Kong
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) upon audit or field inspection; registered principal place of business is the physical location of records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Rolling obligation for a minimum of 7 years from completion of each transaction; accounting records and supporting vouchers must be kept in a form enabling HK profits tax liability to be readily ascertained.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to keep adequate records under Section 51C of the Inland Revenue Ordinance can lead to a fine of up to HK$100,000 (USD 12,800.00) and imprisonment for up to one year; the Commissioner may also make estimated assessments from available material and impose default penalties, which may lead to administrative strike-off where the FIP is treated as not genuinely carrying on business.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Hong Kong Foreign-Invested Partnership is not automatically required to appoint a certified public accountant auditor merely by reason of its partnership status. However, the Inland Revenue Department requires certified audited financial statements, prepared by a certified public accountant (practising), where the partnership's gross income in the relevant basis period is HK$5,000,000 (approximately USD 640,000) or more, where an offshore profits exclusion is claimed, or where the IRD expressly issues a notice requiring audited accounts. If the FIP has a corporate general partner that is a Hong Kong-incorporated company, that corporate partner is subject to the Companies Ordinance Cap. 622 audit mandate unless it qualifies as a small private company. A small private company is one satisfying at least two of the following three quantitative tests: total annual revenue not exceeding HK$10,000,000; total assets not exceeding HK$10,000,000; and 50 or fewer employees. If the corporate partner fails the small-company test, it must be audited in accordance with HKFRS and the applicable Companies Ordinance provisions. In addition, an independent CPA audit is contractually required by most licensed banks supporting Swift_LC, TT_Wire, and XT_Transfer rails for any re-invoicing partnership with annual gross throughput in excess of HK$10,000,000 (approximately USD 1,280,000), given the medium-risk enhanced AML profile.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) as fully converged with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); eligible private entities may apply HKFRS for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE), the SME standard accepted by the Inland Revenue Department provided it gives a true and fair view and is supplemented by all necessary tax computations and disclosures.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong imposes no public UBO annual return on a Foreign-Invested Partnership, but the Limited Partnerships Ordinance requires a registered limited partnership to notify the Companies Registry within 7 days of changes in general partner, limited partner, capital contribution, firm name, or principal place of business. Separately, the Business Registration Office requires changes in business registration particulars to be filed within one month. For this CN_FIP re-invoicing structure, the registered office and licensed banks will require an annual beneficial-ownership confirmation and a 30-day refresh window on any transfer of partnership interests; the medium-risk enhanced AML tier mandates that material changes in partners or controllers be reported to the DNFBP agent before payment rails are reactivated. This annual confirmation is not filed on a public register but is retained in the statutory books and made available for inspection by the IRD, the Companies Registry, and AML supervisors upon request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (counterpart of the Register of Members for partnership interests)
General Partner / Director Appointment Register (where a corporate general partner is used)
Register of Charges and Encumbrances over Partnership Assets
Register of Partnership Capital Contributions, Withdrawals, and Profit/Loss Allocations
Minute Book containing Partner Resolutions and Trade Mandate for LC, TT, and XT Payment Rails

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (PRC standard CIT rate; the FIP itself is a pass-through partnership, so the headline rate applies at the level of the corporate/non-resident partners)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The PRC grants no entity-level CIT holiday to partnerships because the FIP is transparent; however, eligible partners may claim the 15% High and New Technology Enterprise rate, the reduced small low-profit enterprise effective rates for taxable income up to RMB 3 million, 100% R&D super deduction for qualifying outlays, and certain software/integrated-circuit holidays. A Hong Kong corporate partner may also rely on the Hong Kong territorial/offshore profits exemption for profits sourced outside Hong Kong. There is no PRC patent box regime applicable to this re-invoicing trade.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, Category A Main Form A100000, filed through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax electronic filing system; the transparent FIP does not itself file a CIT return, but its corporate partners must include their allocated partnership profits on their CIT returns, and the FIP must file separate partnership information reports as required
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly provisional CIT filings by corporate partners
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual CIT return is due within 5 months of the fiscal year-end (for calendar-year taxpayers, by 31 May of the following year); quarterly advance filings are due within 15 days of each quarter-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue, including gross invoiced turnover from commercial re-invoicing and offshore trade intermediation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full contract value of goods or services purchased and resold through the FIP; do not net intercompany costs against revenue. Cross-border re-invoicing must be supported by the underlying sale contracts, purchase orders, invoices, shipping documents, and payment flows. For a non-resident corporate partner, this gross revenue line is relevant to determining China-source business profits and the possible attribution of profits to a permanent establishment in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating cost, principally the cost of goods sold and direct intercompany purchase costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only costs that are actually incurred, supported by valid vouchers, and consistent with the arm’s length principle. If a related Hong Kong supplier charges an excessive resale price, the tax authority may recharacterize or adjust the transaction under CIT Law Article 41. Prepare and retain a transfer pricing Local File if the related-party tangible property threshold of RMB 200 million is exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit or gross margin after cost of goods sold
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a low-risk re-invoicing hub, a routine wholesale/trading gross margin in the range of 3-8% is typical. If the reported margin falls outside the interquartile range of the benchmark study, the taxpayer must expect adjustment. The margin must reflect the functions performed, assets used, and risks assumed by the FIP, not the profits of the Hong Kong principal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, administrative, and other operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party management fees, royalties, service fees, insurance, and allocated headquarters costs must satisfy economic substance, genuine business purpose, and arm’s length conditions. These items must be disclosed in the annual related-party transaction schedules. If an expense is paid to a non-resident without withholding tax or treaty support, it will be disallowed and additional WHT may be assessed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax, followed by allocation to partners under the partnership agreement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because the FIP is a transparent partnership, the entity-level net profit is allocated to each partner according to the partnership agreement and actual distribution pattern. A Hong Kong corporate partner must report its distributive share of the FIP’s China-source income on its own PRC CIT return. If the HK partner has a permanent establishment in China through the FIP, the share is taxed on a net basis at 25%; if no PE exists and the income is passive in character, a final 10% withholding may apply, subject to treaty protection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments, including transfer pricing add-backs, thin-capitalization interest disallowance, treaty override adjustments, and GAAR recharacterizations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-arm’s length payments, excessive royalty deductions, management fees lacking real services, disallowed interest exceeding the debt-equity ratio under CIT Law Article 46, and any amounts recharacterized under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule in Article 47. For HK treaty relief, verify that the Hong Kong partner is the beneficial owner and has substance; otherwise treaty benefits will be denied and the WHT difference plus penalties imposed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return attracts a penalty up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000-10,000 for serious circumstances under the Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 62. Late payment incurs a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax under Article 32. Under-declaration or fraudulent filing constitutes tax evasion under Article 63, subject to confiscation of illegal gains and a penalty of 50%-500% of the evaded tax. Criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 can lead to imprisonment up to 7 years and monetary fines; fraudulent document/invoice issuance under Article 205 carries severe penalties. Unpaid tax liabilities may trigger exit restrictions and blacklisting.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory PRC withholding tax on dividends paid by a PRC resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise. For a pass-through FIP, profit remittances to partners are not classic dividends; the partner is taxed on its distributive share of China-source business profits. Under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA, dividend-type payments from a PRC resident to a Hong Kong beneficial-owner company are reduced to 5% where that company directly holds at least 25% of the capital of the paying entity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the Hong Kong partner must: (1) obtain an Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Inland Revenue Department for the relevant year; (2) file the PRC Non-Resident Enterprise Treaty Benefit Report through the e-Tax system before or at the time of payment; (3) provide the certificate of incorporation, shareholding register, and evidence of the 25% direct capital holding; (4) submit a beneficial ownership declaration supported by economic substance in Hong Kong, including office, staff, board decisions, bank accounts, and Core Income-Generating Activities; (5) retain contemporaneous proof that the recipient is not a shell or conduit and has the right to the income. The payer may withhold at the reduced treaty rate only after the treaty filing is validated; over-withheld tax may be reclaimed within three years under Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 51.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The PRC statutory gross-basis withholding rate for outbound interest and royalties
